newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Minister warns Hungary farmers over blockade.
newsitem.headline: Minister warns Hungary farmers over blockade.

text.p: Hungary's Interior Minister on Wednesday repeated government warnings that police would prevent one of the country's farmers' unions from carrying out a threat to block border crossings.
Interior Minister Gabor Kuncze told Hungarian radio he still hoped there would be no need for police action, but said they would maintain order if necessary.

The METESZ union sent the government an ultimatum on Monday saying it would set up blockades at Hungary's border crossings and on roads leading into Budapest unless their demand for unconditional tax relief for farmers earning less than 1.5 million forints ($8,500) a year was met.
Government spokesman Elemer Kiss said on Tuesday such action would be both unconstitutional and illegal. Police would clear the roads should the farmers go ahead with their plan, he added.

METESZ leaders said they would start erecting road-blocks at border crossings leading to all neighbouring countries unless their demands were met by Thursday evening, despite the government's warning.
A February demonstration in the central Hungarian town of Kiskoros sparked a series of farmers' protests following income and social security tax increases for individual farmers.

Prime Minister Gyula Horn has ceded to farmers' union demands for round-table talks to solve the crisis of the agriculture sector. He announced on Tuesday that the talks would take place on April 25 to 27.
Hungary has around 30 farmers' unions which sometimes have conflicting interests regarding land ownership, taxation and subsidy issues.
